A1.justification: Both complete 35-page PDFs describe BanditSpec and contain corresponding main sections, algorithms, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–G. The material supports reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original decoding experiments in Section 6, Table 1 and Figure 3, plus memory measurements, larger-model experiments and hardware comparisons in Appendix G.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in Section 6 and Appendix G, including throughput, accepted-token and memory measurements.

M1.justification: BANDITSPEC, UCBSPEC and EXP3SPEC retain the same selection rules, updates and stopping procedures in Algorithms 3–5 and 8–9. The edits do not change the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate draft-model selection on Spec Bench, Alpaca, Code Editor and Debug Bench, and batched speculation-length selection on Alpaca. No dataset, task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains Vanilla, PLD, Rest, Suffix Tree and Eagle-2. Figure 3 retains the same fixed-length, canonical-decoding and oracle/worst comparisons using Eagle-1; Appendix G retains Eagle-2 comparisons.

E3.justification: The target models, metrics and protocols remain unchanged: A100 draft-selection tests with batch size 1, Alpaca batches of 1–50, and speculation lengths 0–4. Appendix G retains the same larger-model and RTX 4090 settings.

E4.justification: The memory and bandwidth analysis in Appendix G.1 and hardware robustness checks in G.3 are retained unchanged. No ablation, sensitivity test, error analysis or case study is added or removed.

E5.justification: Section 6.2 still reports averaging over 16 independent runs; this sentence merely shifts across a page boundary. No new empirical uncertainty estimates, significance tests or seed information appear.

E6.justification: Values and rankings in Tables 1–4, Figure 3 curves and reported findings are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains 105.72 tokens/s for UCBSPEC and 98.15 for Eagle-2 on LLaMA3-8B-Instruct with Spec Bench.

T1.justification: The stopping-time regret definition, assumptions, bounds and proofs in Sections 3–5 and Appendices C–F are mathematically unchanged. Changing 'a random' to 'a random variable' in Appendix D.2 repairs explanatory prose without changing the argument.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about training-free adaptive selection, stopping-time regret guarantees, UCBSPEC optimality and near-oracle throughput.

C2.justification: Both retain the interpretation favoring stationary rewards, the computational tradeoff with KL-UCB, the discussion of adaptive adversaries, and proposed structured, robust and contextual bandit extensions. No substantive limitation or qualification changes.

D1.justification: Hardware specifications, memory disclosures, hyperparameters, the short-response Mixture-of-Agent procedure in Appendix G.1 and the code-access link remain unchanged. Capitalizing 'Python' adds no implementation information.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning remain unchanged, including Appendix A and the SpecDec++ discussion in B.4. Related-work edits correct grammar without revising comparisons or novelty claims.

P1.justification: Localized proofreading spans the main text and appendices, including 'SPECUATIVE' to 'SPECULATIVE' in Algorithm 2 and grammatical repairs in proof explanations. Yunlong Hou's dagger footnote marker is removed; section order and narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: The author block and several column/page breaks reflow; Assumption 5.1 now fits together in the left column of page 6. Figure 2's caption corrects 'repectively', while figure designs, plotted curves and table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves readability through corrected algorithm/caption spelling, grammatical repairs in proof explanations and keeping Assumption 5.1 together. Small introduced slips, such as 'andthe' in Appendix D.2, limit the polish. The gains are editorial; scientific content, empirical support and reproducibility information remain unchanged.
